summary: Malawi admits citizens of 42 countries and territories visa-free, according to the eligibility wizard on its official eVisa portal (as of 8 October 2026). Since February 2026 the US, UK, EU and most other passports can get a visa on arrival, while a list of Category One countries must obtain a visa before departure through the official eVisa portal.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. WHO's country list gives the requirement for travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission, and for travellers who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country.

currencyLimits.text: No Malawian source we could read states a currency rule. notes: The Government of Canada says it is illegal to import or export drugs, pornographic material or ivory, that a licence is needed to import firearms and ammunition for hunting, and that buying or exporting uncut precious stones is illegal.
The Government of Canada says you must declare all foreign currency on arrival and departure, and that the authorities may detain you or confiscate your passport if you do not.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says the economy is predominantly cash-based, US dollars are widely accepted, and credit and debit cards are not widely accepted outside tourist establishments. It adds that you must declare all foreign currency on arrival and departure.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says there is a risk of mugging and bag-snatching, that most thefts from tourists take place around the main bus stations in urban areas, and that there are occasional reports of kidnappings for ransom. It advises avoiding road travel after dark.

tips.text: TravelHealthPro (NaTHNaC) says there is a risk of schistosomiasis (bilharzia) in Malawi and advises all travellers to avoid wading, swimming or bathing in fresh water.
TravelHealthPro (NaTHNaC) says there is a high risk of malaria in Malawi and recommends antimalarial tablets. It advises mosquito bite avoidance.
The Government of Canada says US dollars are widely accepted and that you must declare all foreign currency on arrival and departure.
The UK FCDO says there are frequent fuel shortages, often with long queues. It advises not assuming fuel will be available on your route and planning ahead to reach your destination.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Malawi?
faq.answer: Most visitors do. Citizens of 42 countries and territories — including South Africa, Zambia, Kenya, Ghana and Singapore — enter visa-free, according to the eVisa portal's eligibility wizard (as of 8 October 2026). Citizens of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, the EU and most other countries can buy a visa on arrival (USD 50 for a single entry, according to the UK Foreign Office) or apply in advance at evisa.gov.mw, while Category One countries such as India, China and Nigeria must get a visa before departure.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Malawi and can I extend?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how many days a single-entry visa allows. The Government of Canada says that to stay longer you should contact Malawi's Department of Immigration and Citizenship Services, and that you may be fined on departure if you overstay. No official source we could read says where an extension is granted or for how long.

faq.question: Can I still get a Malawi visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, for nationals of the Category Two countries, which include the US, UK, Canada, Australia and the EU: a public notice effective 24 February 2026 makes them eligible at all designated ports of entry, and tells airlines to board them without a visa. The UK FCDO advises bringing US dollars in cash. Category One nationals must still obtain a visa before departure, and the government encourages everyone to apply in advance at evisa.gov.mw.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Malawi?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission (UK Foreign Office and WHO), or, according to WHO's country list, transited for more than 12 hours through an airport of such a country.

faq.question: Is it safe to swim in Lake Malawi?
faq.answer: TravelHealthPro (NaTHNaC) says there is a risk of schistosomiasis (bilharzia) in Malawi and advises all travellers to avoid wading, swimming or bathing in fresh water.
